Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-03 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reading)

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification or reading for this
fragment. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..032 in packet-03 (and listed the directory).
I did not open packet.json and used no search. I have not tried to identify the work or
author. The only external text seen is the modern pencil shelfmark on the parchment
("Stams, STA, Frg. 187r" / "187v") and a later ink mark "B 98" on the spine fold.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observations)
- Two overviews: image-001 (face pencilled "Frg. 187r") and image-017 ("Frg. 187v").
  Tiles image-002..016 belong to 187r; image-018..032 to 187v.
- Parchment bifolium (two leaves joined at a central fold), opened flat, used as a binding
  wrapper: corners cut diagonally, turn-ins at top and bottom, sewing slits along the fold,
  later "F" label on a pasted paper slip and "B 98" in ink on the fold (187r).
- Each leaf: two columns, about 40 lines per column, small Caroline/early Gothic book hand
  in brown ink. Upright orientation.
- Red underlining marks lemma text (quoted base text) inside the prose; lemmata start with
  enlarged ink capitals (some touched with red, e.g. "Et vocavit" with a red paraph).
  Red paragraph marks before some lemmata.
- In the outer and inner margins: red abbreviations "ag", "c", "ca", once "ag let" (?),
  each often followed by a vertical red line running down beside several lines.
  Tentative interpretation: source/attribution markers for passages of commentary.
- Small interlinear marks (double-stroke "construe"/reference signs, some in red) over words.
- Tentative interpretation: a continuous Latin commentary on a scriptural text, with lemmata
  underlined in red and section markers ("Tercia pars", "Quarta pars", "Secunda pars").
- Damage: water staining and darkening at the fold and lower right of 187r; 187v very
  stained in the right leaf's second column (middle) and left leaf's second column (bottom).
  Bottom 1-2 lines of each column often faded.

SPANS SELECTED: I read substantial runs in all eight columns. Lemmata (red-underlined) are
marked [LEMMA]. Unread/omitted: the first, very faint top line of most columns; the most
stained middle lines of 187v right leaf col b; some line ends at the fold.
Conventions: (expansion), word? = uncertain, [illegible], [..] = lost/unread portion.
Line numbers count visible text lines from the top of the named tile. Tiles overlap: where
a line appears in two tiles I give it once and note the overlap.

LIMITATIONS
- This is an unverified first reading. Abbreviation density is high; many expansions are
  conjectural and marked "?". Several readings were made against cropped tiles where the
  line start or end is in a neighbouring tile; I stitched them by overlap.
- Top line of every column is faint/rubbed (turn-in area) and mostly unread.
- 187v right leaf col b, middle lines (around "Op(us) .n. q(uo)d mandat(ur)"), and 187v left
  leaf col b bottom lines are heavily stained; readings there are weakest.
- 187r right leaf col a middle lines (image-010 l.5-7) are in darker ink, possibly retraced
  or a different hand; content there uncertain.
- Column order: within each face I read left leaf col a, col b, then right leaf col a, col b.
  Which leaf precedes in the original book is not determinable from these images alone; the
  bifolium may be a nested sheet, so text may not run directly from the left leaf to the
  right leaf on the same face.
- Marginal red letters ("ag", "c", "ca") are transcribed only in the survey, not per line.
